reasons.A: Period diction (to-day, practise) and dry aphorisms fit, but its irony is sharper and more epigrammatic than the passage's easy, genial mockery, and its sentences are more uniformly balanced.
reasons.B: Modern register and idiom (more to the point, started a business, raised a child) with brisk, plain sentences; argues earnestly rather than with the passage's leisurely, gently ironic period voice.
reasons.C: Closest to the passage's genial, amused irony and homely illustration; 'Now it must be confessed' movement, mixed long and short sentences and period diction feel native, though its questions and one exclamation are slightly more than the passage uses.
